route.description: Approved Route 2 has two segments. Segment 2A runs ~39 miles generally north from the Tremval Substation Expansion North (Larkin Valley) site near Blair to the new Elk Farm Substation in the Town of Seymour. Segment 2B runs ~41 miles: east, then north along North 90th Avenue toward STH 29, then east along the STH 29 corridor beside an existing line to Jump River Substation South in the Town of Longwood, Clark County.
route.caveat: schematic / not survey accurate. Waypoints are vertices of the Route 2 polylines (layer 39 'Transmission Route') in the PSC's docket 5-CE-158 map service, simplified with a 150 m tolerance (max deviation checked: 136 m on 2A, 122 m on 2B). This is application/proceeding-era GIS for the route the Commission authorized 'as presented'. The local alternatives in the map-service layers 'Route Adjustment 11.5' (near 190th/195th/199th Street, within about 1.5 km of the plotted line) and 'Route Adjustment 11.7' (PSCW-KF-11.7) were not merged. NSPW's Q2 2026 report says pole spotting between Elk Farm and Larkin Valley was completed in June 2026, but the 30% design package was still in progress and pole spotting for Elk Farm to Jump River was preliminary, so the final alignment may shift.

knownCoordination.description: Dairyland's Alma-Blair 345 kV line terminates at the new Tremval North switching station approved in 5-CE-158. Dairyland's July 2024 application said the final connection configuration would be 'determined in coordination with Xcel Energy', and that the station must be completed by the end of 2028 for Dairyland's connection. Dairyland was a granted intervenor in 5-CE-158 but offered no evidence. This is interconnection-level coordination only; no source documents shared crews, equipment or construction sequencing.

Both PSC final decisions name the Tremval Substation Expansion North: WWTC is certificated with that site, and the Grid Forward (5-CE-157) construction sequence is described as beginning there, with its route exiting it. NSPW and ATC applied for both projects; Grid Forward also lists SMMPA Wisconsin and WPPI Energy as applicants. The applicants stated that each project provides benefits individually and in conjunction with the other. No reviewed source says how Tremval-site work is split between the two dockets or documents shared construction resources. Because the owners overlap, this pair is shared-owner context, not a cross-utility lead.

unresolved: plan.md hypothesis check: 'Planned construction in 2026-27' is supported only by Xcel's web page ('Construction : 2026 -2027') and its Jan 2026 info sheet. The PSC final decision (start Q3 2026, completion by Q3 2029) and NSPW's Q2 2026 filing (start Q4 2026, in-service Q3 2029) imply construction running into 2029. 'Near the Dairyland project around Blair' is supported: the Alma-Blair line terminates at WWTC's Tremval North / Larkin Valley station.

Minnesota / Mississippi River end: no WWTC source describes one. WWTC runs entirely inside Wisconsin (Trempealeau, Eau Claire, Chippewa and Clark counties), from Larkin Valley/Tremval North near Blair to Jump River South. Xcel only mentions other projects 'proposed in Minnesota and to the west'. Any Mississippi crossing toward Alma belongs to other projects (e.g., Dairyland Alma-Blair).

Eau Claire Substation expansion: the docket caption still lists 'Expanding the Tremval and Eau Claire Substations', but the Eau Claire expansion was part of Route 1. The authorized Route 2 uses the new Elk Farm Substation instead, and NSPW's Q2 2026 cost table lists only Larkin Valley and Elk Farm substations. No source confirms any remaining Eau Claire Substation work under 5-CE-158.

Completion conflict (not reconciled): the Xcel web page ('Project complete: 2027 - 2028') and the Jan 2026 info sheet ('Project complete and line placed in service', 2027-2028) disagree with the PSC final decision and case page ('completion by the third quarter of 2029') and with NSPW's own Q2 2026 filing ('in-service date of third quarter 2029').

Construction start moved across claims: Q3 2025 (application era, PSC case page), then Q3 2026 (final decision), then Q4 2026 (NSPW Q2 2026 report). ATC's Jump River Substation is set for Q3 2027. The Xcel web page and info sheet show construction in 2026-2027, which conflicts with a Q3 2029 in-service date.

Removed as superseded: the PSC case page's application-era schedule ('If approved, the applicant anticipates construction for this project to begin in the third quarter of 2025 and be in-service in the third quarter of 2029') is not listed as a construction window. The same page gives the later final-decision schedule, and NSPW's Q2 2026 report shows construction had not started by mid-2026. The output schema has no supersededBy field. Its in-service claim (Q3 2029) is kept in completionClaims.

Removed from the ATC package: the final decision's project-wide schedule (construction from Q3 2026, completion by Q3 2029) is not specific to the Jump River Substation. ATC's own Q2 2026 report gives a package-specific start of Q3 2027.

Window end bounds: no source gives an explicit construction end date for NSPW's or ATC's work. The PSC and NSPW windows end at the stated completion or in-service quarter. ATC's window ends at the overall Project in-service quarter and is marked non-continuous. 'Completion by the third quarter of 2029' is encoded as Q3 2029, though 'by' permits an earlier finish.

Whether construction had actually started by 2026-09-26 is not confirmed. The latest filings are the Q2 2026 progress reports (filed July 27 and July 31, 2026), and a web search found no later construction-start notice. Q3 2026 reports are due after the quarter ends.

PSC final decision cost table (p. 52): the Route 2 transmission line and 'Other T-Line Removal/Installation' costs are labeled 'ATC'. NSPW's Q2 2026 report says this is wrong and that NSPW constructs the line. No corrected PSC table was found. The NSPW table ($438.8M) and ATC's table ($44.511M) together make up the $483.3M total.

ATC scope vs NSPW's statement: NSPW says it will 'construct, own and operate all parts of the project except the Jump River Substation'. ATC's image-only cost table (Q2 2026 report p.3, read visually, not script-verifiable) lists ATC 'Transmission Lines - South (Route 2)' ($5,745,000) and items at Gardner Park and Stone Lake substations. What that line and remote-substation work is, and where, was not determined; those sites are not mapped.

Final order date: the Xcel web page says December 11, 2025 and the Jan 2026 info sheet says December 10, 2025. The decision is signed December 10, 2025 and was PSC-received/served December 11, 2025. Xcel says verbal approval came October 30, 2025.

Docket numbering: Dairyland's July 2024 application calls WWTC 'PSCW Docket No. 4220-CE-188', while the PSC decision, the case page and the progress reports use joint docket 5-CE-158. No cached source states the renumbering; the mapping rests on the identical project name.
The PSC case page link text reads 'Docket Reports: 5-CE-185', but the link points to the ERF search for docket 5-CE-158 (SEQ=158). Treated as a typo.
ATC's Q2 2026 report says its period is 'April 1, through June 30, 2025'. Treated as a typo for 2026.

Internal text conflict in the final decision: p.15 says that after leaving W3305, Route 2 travels 'north in a single-circuit configuration for 27 miles'. p.33 says Segment 2B 'would generally parallel the existing transmission line' for about 27 miles. The PSC GIS polyline runs almost due east (about lat 44.92) from the STH 29 crossing to Jump River South, and Xcel says it generally follows State Highway 29. The GIS geometry is used.

Route geometry comes from the PSC docket map service (layer 39 'Transmission Route', application/proceeding-era GIS). The Commission approved Route 2 'as presented', but the adjustment layers 'Route Adjustment 11.5' (190th/195th/199th Street alternatives near the STH 29 crossing) and 'Route Adjustment 11.7' (PSCW-KF-11.7), the 'Structure N1-120 Option' layer, and final engineering could shift the alignment. No post-decision as-designed GIS was found. The layer list came from a live query and is not cached.
The crossing points at 250th Street (Town of Sigel) and 370th Street (Edson/Worden border) were not geocoded separately; the GIS polyline, which passes through those towns, is used instead.

Schedule dependency (not reconciled): Dairyland's July 2024 application says the new switching station must be completed by the end of 2028 for Dairyland's connection, and the 1515-CE-103 decision gives Alma-Blair a September 2028 in-service date. WWTC sources give only whole-project completion/in-service dates (Q3 2029, or 2027-2028 per Xcel) and no separate completion date for the Larkin Valley / Tremval North station.

No reviewed source documents resource sharing (crews, equipment, laydown yards, outage or construction sequencing) between NSPW and Dairyland, or between WWTC and Grid Forward. Resource-sharing status is 'not found in sources', which is not the same as 'uncoordinated'.

Owner overlap with Grid Forward: NSPW and ATC are applicants for both WWTC and Grid Forward (5-CE-157, with SMMPA and WPPI). Under plan.md section 8, a WWTC vs Grid Forward pair is shared-owner context, not a cross-utility review lead. Grid Forward also describes 'expanding the Tremval Substation', and how Tremval North / Larkin Valley work is split between 5-CE-157 and 5-CE-158 was not determined.

Cross-cluster coordinate mismatch: the Dairyland cluster places the same Tremval North switching station at the Blair locality centroid (44.2946, -91.2338, precision locality). The PSC GIS point 'Tremval Expansion North' (44.30158, -91.25420) is about 1.8 km away and should be preferred when the clusters are merged.

The Xcel Jan 2026 info-sheet schedule excerpt contains U+0007 (BEL) control characters from the PDF text layer. They are kept verbatim so the excerpt checker can match it; the UI may need to strip them for display.
psc-wwtc-map (the PSC project map PDF) is image-only with no text layer. It was used only to check the GIS route visually and cannot anchor excerpts.

Only NSPW's Q2 2026 report assigns 'Other T-Line Removal/Installation' (rebuilds of existing lines, $29.2M PSC-approved) to NSPW. Which existing lines are rebuilt (the final decision names W3305 and 3418 near the STH 29 crossing, and W3203 on the common segment), and who owns them, was not fully extracted.
The MISO LRTP Tranche 1 Project 5 documents themselves were not consulted. The parent-initiative label rests on the PSC final decision caption and text and on the PSC case page.
